newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania gets crude for Iran's outstanding debt.
newsitem.headline: Romania gets crude for Iran's outstanding debt.

text.p: Romania has agreed to accept crude and fuel oil to cover part of an outstanding Iranian debt and intends to do the same with Egypt, a Romanian oil trader said on Friday.
"Iranian oil imports, worth $26 million, amount to 131,000 tonnes and will reach (the Black Sea port of) Constanta around December 22," Valeriu Iancu, Petrolexportimport SA manager, told Reuters.

He said Iran had already sent 43,000 tonnes of fuel oil, worth around $6.0 million, intended for the electricity authority Renel RA. Iran's outstanding debts, dating from before the 1989 execution of Romania's dictator Nicolae Ceausescu, stand at $43 million.
"We are now discussing recovery of a $33 million debt from Egypt, with $22 million in the immediate future and another $11 million in January," Iancu said.
He said Egypt would send around 130,000 tonnes of crude oil to Romania. Last year Romania had recovered $75 million from Egypt in around 550,000 tonnes of crude, he added.
Iancu said Petrolexportimport had also guaranteed letters of credit worth a total $39 million, issued by Societe Generale and Banca Franco-Romana SA commercial bank.
"The money will finance oil imports," he said.

Romania, which has seen crude extraction drop to annual levels of around 6.7 million tonnes from peaks of 14 million tonnes in the 1970s, must import meet domestic demand and keep its 12 refineries operating.

State-run Petrolexportimport, the country's sole crude and oil products trader, said it had imported around 8.5 million tonnes of crude so far this year. -- Luli Popescu, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
